directAnswer: Boniface II was pope from 530 to 532 and the first pope of Germanic descent; he was born in Rome to a father with a Gothic name. Designated by Felix IV, he faced the rival candidate Dioscorus until Dioscorus died weeks later. Boniface confirmed the canons of the Second Council of Orange on grace.

paras: Felix IV, near death, named the archdeacon Boniface as his successor. The majority of the Roman clergy, rejecting this unprecedented designation, elected the deacon Dioscorus. Both were consecrated on September 22, 530.

Dioscorus died on October 14, leaving Boniface unopposed. Boniface required the clergy who had supported his rival to sign a condemnation of Dioscorus's memory. Later he tried to name the deacon Vigilius as his own successor at a Roman synod, but opposition forced him to withdraw and burn the decree.

sections.h2: Orange and the Anno Domini Question
paras: In 531, Boniface wrote to Caesarius of Arles approving the canons of the Second Council of Orange, which taught that the beginning of faith is itself a gift of grace. The Liber Pontificalis also says he helped relieve the clergy during a famine.

Some popular lists credit Boniface with changing the way years were numbered. The Anno Domini count came from the Easter tables of Dionysius Exiguus in 525, before Boniface was pope; his own role in its adoption is not established. Boniface died in October 532. He is not venerated as a saint.

keyFacts: Pope from 530 to 532; first pope of Germanic descent
Designated by Felix IV; contested by Dioscorus until Dioscorus died
Attempted, then withdrew, the designation of Vigilius as successor
Confirmed the Second Council of Orange's teaching on grace in 531

faqs.question: Why is Boniface II called the first Germanic pope?
faqs.answer: He was born in Rome, but his father bore a Gothic name, which is why he is considered the first pope of Germanic ancestry.

faqs.question: Did Pope Boniface II introduce Anno Domini dating?
faqs.answer: No clear evidence supports that. The Anno Domini system came from Dionysius Exiguus's Easter tables, written in 525, before Boniface became pope.
